en: The Section on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra)
He who fully understands the eye-base has fully understood the ear-base? No.
Or rather, he who has fully understood the ear-base fully understands the eye-base? No.
He who does not fully understand the eye-base has not fully understood the ear-base?
An Arahant does not fully understand the eye-base, but he has not failed to fully understand the ear-base.
With the exception of one who possesses the highest path (the Arahant) and the Arahant himself, all remaining persons do not fully understand the eye-base and have not fully understood the ear-base.
Or, conversely: whoever has not fully understood the ear-base, does he not fully understand the eye-base?
One who possesses the highest path has not fully understood the ear-base, but does not fail to fully understand the eye-base.
With the exception of one who possesses the highest path and an Arahant, all remaining persons have neither fully understood the ear-base nor do they fully understand the eye-base.
